    Two-ended negative boundary squares for string modules #

    The double-peak Butler--Ringel sequence is obtained by attaching a negative boundary at both ends of a shorter string. The right-module maps are inclusions. This file proves that any coherent common-corner square of those inclusions gives the canonical exact complex from the base to the two one-ended extensions and then to the common corner.
